summary: p95 latency of LLM calls rose from 0.2375s to 4.875s while 5xx ratio and queue depth stayed at 0; onset (first elevated sample 2026-09-29T19:22:00Z) follows a Deployment rollout of insighthub-api at 19:20:29Z that added env CHAOS_LLM_DELAY_SECONDS=4 and a /chaos configmap mount, and latency returned to baseline at 19:32:29Z after rollback to the previous ReplicaSet at 19:27:58Z (ALERTS pending 19:22:29Z, firing 19:24:29Z-19:31:29Z).
root_cause: Rollout of Deployment insighthub-api at 2026-09-29T19:20:29Z to ReplicaSet insighthub-api-775bb6dfcb (revision 3), whose pod template injected env CHAOS_LLM_DELAY_SECONDS=4, PYTHONPATH=/chaos and a configmap volume chaos-llm-latency (same image insighthub/api:1007430) - an artificial ~4s delay on each LLM call; rolled back at 19:27:58Z to ReplicaSet insighthub-api-776f558c which has none of these.
confidence_reason: Two independent signals agree: application metric (LLM p95 0.2375 -> 4.875, tracks the delay of 4s and reverts after rollback) and Kubernetes signals (Deployment/ReplicaSet events and ReplicaSet spec with the delay env var, plus api available replicas dipping to 0 during rollback). More than two alternative hypotheses were ruled out with metrics. Not higher because the in-pod code path applying the delay was not inspected and the request-rate increase is unexplained.

Add a rollout-diff alert/guard on env changes to api Deployment coinciding with LLM p95 anomalies (tied to hypotheses on kube_deployment_status_replicas_available and onset at 19:22:00Z)
Investigate the request-rate rise (tied to the http_requests:rate5m hypotheses) before closing

injected_fault.name: llm-latency
injected_fault.mechanism: sitecustomize.py mounted from ConfigMap chaos-llm-latency wraps app.services.llm.generate with time.sleep(4); enabled by env CHAOS_LLM_DELAY_SECONDS=4 and PYTHONPATH=/chaos on Deployment insighthub-api (rollout revision 3). The lab runs RAG_MODE=fixture, so this is injected delay, not a slow real provider.
injected_fault.traffic_during_fault: the script drove POST /chat every ~2s (recovery phase every ~5s) on top of the baseline load generator

injected_fault_evaluation.detail: The blind investigator identified the api Deployment rollout at 19:20:29Z that added CHAOS_LLM_DELAY_SECONDS=4, PYTHONPATH=/chaos and the chaos-llm-latency ConfigMap, the ~4s delay per LLM call, and the rollback at 19:27:58Z; timings match the script log. Caveats: (1) the fault is self-labelled in the pod spec (env/ConfigMap names), so identification was a spec diff more than inference, and the code path of the delay was not inspected; (2) the unexplained request-rate rise it flagged is the chaos script own traffic driver; (3) the api availability dip to 0 replicas at rollout/rollback is the maxSurge=0 strategy patch needed on this 2-CPU node, not part of the injected fault; (4) CPU throttling was left unverified, not ruled out.

investigation_window_note: started_at is 15 min before the fault (baseline), ended_at is after the alert resolved; samples must fall inside this window (verify.py:618).
rca_method: Independent subagent with no session context and no knowledge of the injected fault; Prometheus MCP + Kubernetes MCP; samples verbatim from scripts/chaos/harvest-samples.py; prompt: observability/rca-prompt.md. hypotheses/ruled_out/samples are unedited subagent output.
